story: My employer in Jaipur has not paid my salary for September 2026, Rs 28,000.

timeline.user_words: My employer in Jaipur has not paid my salary for September 2026, Rs 28,000.

facts.user_goal: Get the unpaid salary of Rs 28,000 for September 2026.

rules.name: monthly_due_date
rules.message: Wages for September 2026 were due before the end of 07 October 2026 (the 7th of the next month).
rules.label: When wages were due

rules.name: wage_claim_limitation
rules.message: File your wage claim before 07 Oct 2029 (1064 days left). This counts 3 years from 07 Oct 2026 (when September 2026 wages fell due; each later month has its own, later deadline). Don't wait for the last date.
rules.label: Last date to file your wage claim

rules.name: where_to_claim
rules.message: You (or your union) can file a claim before the wage authority. For banks, railways, telecom, mines, insurance and central PSUs this is the Central Government's authority; for other employers it is your State labour department. It can order up to ten times the claim as compensation and recovers unpaid amounts like land revenue. The employer has to prove they paid you.
rules.label: Where to claim

rules.name: amount
rules.message: Unpaid wages: 1 month(s) x Rs 28,000 = Rs 28,000 (before any lawful deductions; HRA and overtime also count as wages for payment).
rules.label: Amount

answer.summary: Your employer in Jaipur did not pay your September 2026 salary of Rs 28,000. The law says wages for a month must be paid by the 7th of the next month. You can file a wage claim to get this money back. The wage authority can order your employer to pay and can even order them to pay up to ten times your claim as extra compensation.

claims.text: Your employer must pay your wages by the 7th of the next month.
Wages include your basic pay and any allowances, like house rent.
Your employer must prove they paid you if you file a claim.
The wage authority can order compensation up to ten times your claim.
Your employer must pay you back within two working days if you are removed, dismissed, or resign.

next_steps.action: Collect proof of your employment and the unpaid month.
next_steps.why: You need evidence to show the wage authority you worked and were not paid.

next_steps.action: File a wage claim with the labour department.
next_steps.why: You can file a claim for your unpaid salary and possible extra compensation.

next_steps.action: Call 15100 for free legal help if you need it.
next_steps.why: You can get free legal advice from the District Legal Services Authority.

support.text: Your employer must pay your wages by the 7th of the next month.
support.reason: The law text in s17(1)(iv) states that for monthly basis employment, wages must be paid 'before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month,' which directly supports the sentence that employer must pay wages by the 7th of the next month.

support.text: Wages include your basic pay and any allowances, like house rent.
support.reason: The law text in s2y explicitly states that house rent allowance is NOT included in wages ('does not include––... (f) house rent allowance'), directly contradicting the sentence that wages include house rent.

support.text: Your employer must prove they paid you if you file a claim.
support.reason: The law text in s59 explicitly states 'the burden to prove that the said dues have been paid shall be on the employer,' directly supporting the sentence that the employer must prove they paid the employee if a claim is filed.

support.text: The wage authority can order compensation up to ten times your claim.
support.reason: The law text in s45(2) explicitly states that the authority 'may order... the payment of compensation in addition to the claim determined, which may extend to ten times of the claim determined,' directly supporting the sentence that the wage authority can order compensation up to ten times the claim.

support.text: Your employer must pay you back within two working days if you are removed, dismissed, or resign.
support.reason: The law text in s17(2) explicitly states that 'the wages payable to him shall be paid within two working days of his removal, dismissal, retrenchment or, as the case may be, his resignation,' directly supporting the sentence.

draft:
Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: [FILL: name of the other party], [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for payment of unpaid wages

I was employed with you at a monthly wage of Rs 28,000. My wages for September 2026 have not been paid.

I request you to pay the unpaid amount of Rs 28,000 within 15 days of receiving this letter, to my bank account [FILL: account details].

If the amount is not paid, I intend to file a claim before the authority under the Code on Wages, 2019, which may also award compensation, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: [FILL: receipts, chats, emails, bank statements].

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in your offer letter, salary slip, or the company's registered office on the MCA website (mca.gov.in).
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Code on Wages, 2019, s.17(1)-(4) (Time limit for payment of wages); Code on Wages, 2019, s.45(1)-(6) (Claims authority, compensation, recovery and time limit); Code on Wages, 2019, s.59 (Burden of proof on employer); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(d) (Central or State Government: whose authority applies); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(y) (main part, clauses (a)-(j)) (What counts as "wages")
